basis: Benign tumour confined to the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Tuberculous infection of the larynx; upper airways belong to the pulmonary axis.
Defined by impaired gastric motility and emptying; no underlying neurologic or metabolic cause is required.
Developmental femoral epiphyseal disease with necrosis, cystic change or sclerosis.
Carcinoma arising in breast parenchyma; breast has no axis.
Pontocerebellar and motor neuron degeneration; denervation muscle atrophy is characteristic/common (>30%). Retinal dystrophy is 5–29%; renal microangiopathy is uncommon.
Uveal melanoma originating in the ciliary body.
Brain, retinal and renal disease define this subtype; hepatic fibrosis occurs in 5/5 annotated patients and cirrhosis in 3/4.
BBS retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and polydactyly; renal disease occurs in roughly 30–50% across BBS. Common neurodevelopmental involvement omitted by cap; subtype data sparse.
NDE1-related cortical malformation with microcephaly, profound developmental impairment and frequent seizures.
Traumatic full-thickness defect of the macula; retinal injury belongs to the ocular axis.
Seminal vesicle inflammation affects a reproductive organ; this generic concept does not establish infection or an autoimmune mechanism.
HHV-8-associated Kaposi sarcoma arising in the rectum; infectious ancestry supports the mechanism axis.
Congenital reduction of the great toe to a single phalanx is a skeletal abnormality.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes bronchiectasis/rhinitis. Hearing loss occurs in 1/1 annotated patient and commonly in PCD (>30%); thyroid disease is not established as intrinsic.
Superficial fascia and subcutaneous tissue are included in the dermatologic axis; other effects vary across subtypes.
Neurologic movement syndrome associated with third-ventricular cysts and hydrocephalus.
Epithelial carcinoma arising in the ovary; reproductive tumour origin does not establish endocrine disease.
The available name identifies fibular hypoplasia and scapulopelvic skeletal dysplasia; no evidence supports additional axes.
B-cell precursor leukemia/lymphoma affects marrow and lymphoid cells; the lymphoma component warrants the infectious_immune axis.
Mitochondrial myopathy directly damages extraocular and eyelid muscles, causing progressive ocular paralysis; systemic features vary by subtype.
Limb shortening and skeletal dysplasia define Robinow syndrome; cardiac, renal and dental abnormalities are annotated at 5–29%.
Food-triggered, non-IgE-mediated immune inflammation of the intestine.
Familial recurrent skeletal muscle cramps; no supplied evidence establishes neuropathy or a metabolic disorder.
Intellectual disability defines disease; strabismus 13/21, blepharophimosis 12/21 and hypermetropia 7/21 support ocular involvement; brachydactyly 12/21 supports skeletal involvement.
